root_cause.text: The function `cgroup_storage_get_next_key()` uses `list_next_entry()` to advance to the next element and then checks if the result is NULL, but `list_next_entry()` never returns NULL—when at the end of the list it wraps to the list head—so the NULL check is dead code, causing the function to read from a bogus pointer (the list head) and copy invalid data to userspace instead of returning -ENOENT.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states: "list_next_entry() never returns NULL -- when the current element is the last entry it wraps to the list head via container_of(). The subsequent NULL check is therefore dead code and get_next_key() never returns -ENOENT for the last element, instead reading storage->key from a bogus pointer that aliases internal map fields and copying the result to userspace." The patch replaces the NULL check with `list_entry_is_head()`.

intent_record.how: The original null check never triggered because list_next_entry never returns NULL; the condition was always false, so the function would incorrectly continue past the list head. The fix properly detects when the iterator has wrapped around to the list head and jumps to enoent, signaling end of iteration.
